transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026
Time: 15:00 PT (PST)
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Priya (Harbor TPM), Mark (Eng Mgr), Jenna (FinOps), Omar (Security)

Auto summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Purpose: QBR-style checkin to sync on adoption, forecast next 6 weeks, and kick off a stability sprint to prepare for expected uptake.
- Outcomes: agree on data handoff, run a stress test, cost sizing sheet, and security questions.

Topics: adoption forecast, cost/run-rate, latency and reliability, dedicated vs hosted routing, batching and KV-cache, security/KMS/SOC2, pilot/stress testing, roadmap alignment

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Okay, hey everyone thanks for carving out time. This is Alex from Redwood, im joined by Samir our SE and Lina from CS. How everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya: Good thanks, busy week but excited. Quick thing, we moved the launch date up so want to validate capacity.
[00:13] Mark: Yeah we saw a bigger-than-expected uptick in beta — about 1.8x week-over-week.
[00:17] Samir: Got it. So the plan for today is to line up telemetry, agree on targets for the stability sprint, and run a small load check. We'll also go through cost tradeoffs — batch sizing, quantizashun impact, etc.
[00:28] Jenna: From finance side, we need a projection. Last month was a surprise spike, we want to avoid another overrun.
[00:33] Alex: Totally. Samir will walk through the run-rate model and then we'll propose a right-sizing with dedicated commit options. Quick note — some of the product names in our docs might show as Reedwood Dedicated in older slides, ignore that.
[00:45] Samir: (screen share) So here's Harbor's token histogram that Lina pulled in earlier. I see a heavy tail for chat completion at ~512 tokens, and a smaller but consistent 2–3% of calls approaching 2k. That matters for KV cache sizing and latency.
[00:59] Priya: Is that from production or staging?
[01:01] Lina: Mixed, about 70% prod, 30% internal staging tests.
[01:05] Samir: Ok, so two immediate levers: prefix caching (KV cache) for repeated contexts, and adaptive batching for lower-priority routes. We can also recommend a quantization profile — 4-bit for most models — to drop cost. There's some quality tradeoff but usually small for classification and templated responses.
[01:22] Mark: For quality we need to keep customer-facing conversations at >=99.2% pass rate on our eval set, so anything that degrades should be gated.
[01:30] Samir: Absolutely, that will be in the right-sizing doc as quality thresholds and rollback instructions.
[01:35] Omar: Security quick pop — what about KMS integration? We need to ensure keys never leave our VPC. Also audit logs and a copy of the SOC2 report.
[01:44] Alex: Good call. We support both Customer-Managed KMS and Redwood-managed keys; for Private deployments we can do in-VPC HSM attachments. We'll send the SOC2 summary and audit log schema after this call.
[01:55] Omar: Also, encryption at rest for KV-store?
[01:57] Samir: Yes encrypted at rest by default; the KV artifact names sometimes come through as K V cache in older transcripts, apologies for the parsing.
[02:04] Priya: Timeline — we have executive review on 2026-06-22. Need a concrete plan before then.
[02:10] Alex: Understood. So 3-week runway. We'll aim to deliver the cost workbook and a pre-stress test checklist next week.
[02:17] Jenna: On cost model, can you show the difference hosted vs dedicated? We prefer hosted but if committed capacity saves 30% we might be open.
[02:25] Samir: On the slide — hosted pay-as-you-go has higher per-token but lower ops overhead; dedicated/reserved commits give 20–35% unit cost savings depending on utilization and whether you accept slightly higher cold-start latency on some variants. Also routing policies can keep low-latency routes on a premium pool while failing over to cheaper quantized variants.
[02:45] Mark: What about autoscaling and burst capacity? We cannot have throttling at peak.
[02:50] Alex: We can configure burst pools and canary rollouts. For hard SLOs we recommend dedicated with a reserved baseline and a burst overlay.
[02:59] Priya: For the stability sprint — what does success look like?
[03:02] Lina: We proposed three KPIs in the pre-meeting notes: 1) P95 latency under 350ms for critical route, 2) no more than 0.5% error rate on inference calls, 3) cost within projected band +/-10%.
[03:14] Priya: Sounds reasonable. Can we get automated alerts if latency drifts?
[03:18] Samir: Yes, Redwood Console supports per-route latency and token-level cost alerts; we can configure thresholds and webhook integrations to your PagerDuty.
[03:26] Mark: A bit of a nit — we have legacy reranking on an older infra, does Redwood support hybrid routing? For ex, some calls still go to our on-prem reranker.
[03:35] Samir: Yes hybrid is supported. We can set routing policies so that reranks hit your on-premers and others go to Redwood. Also can do A/B rollout where 5% stays on legacy during the initial week.
[03:45] Priya: Ok next, stress testing specifics. We want the load to match 2x of last peak over 24h including burst windows. What metrics should we expect?
[03:54] Samir: We'll instrument: tokens/sec, requests/sec, GPU utilization, KV hit-rate, and tail latency; we'll also produce flame charts for any head-of-line blocking.
[04:05] Jenna: Can Redwood share a sample spreadsheet that maps tokens -> cost under different quant profiles?
[04:10] Alex: Yes, we'll attach a workbook. Expect line items: model, variant, q-profile, tokens per call, unit cost, estimated monthly run-rate.
[04:16] Priya: Any blockers for SOC2 scoping?
[04:19] Omar: We need proof of audit logs retention, SSO/SAML integrations, RBAC controls. Also would like to see per-tenant traceability.
[04:27] Lina: We'll get the SOC2 docs, SSO setup guide, and a sample audit-log export.
[04:31] Mark: One more — network egress costs if we route to a different region during failover. That can be expensive.
[04:37] Samir: Good point. We'll include cross-region egress assumptions in the cost model and also show a routing policy that prefers same-region when available.
[04:44] Priya: Ok let's recap so execs get a clean ask.
[04:47] Alex: Recap: Redwood will deliver— right-sizing recommendation + cost workbook by 2026-06-09; schedule stress test (week of 6/14); share SOC2 summary and KMS/HSM integration notes by 6/05; Harbor to provide token histograms & peak traces by 6/07. We'll set up a follow-up checkpoint pre-exec review on 2026-06-16.
[05:10] Priya: That works. Thanks everyone.
[05:13] Jenna: One last thing — please make the cost workbook in a format our FinOps can drop into our internal model (CSV + notes).
[05:20] Alex: Will do. Thanks all, we'll send notes and links in the next 24 hours.

End of transcript.
